definition: In this historical usage, carnal means bodily or physical in a sexual sense. The source contrasts carnal feeling with sexual feeling that is mainly imaginative or emotional.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Erotomania; pinned source text

reasons: The packet (Baldwin 1901) only uses the term “carnal” in a contrast (“sexual feeling is imaginative and emotional rather than carnal”) and does not explicitly state that, in this usage, “carnal means bodily or physical in a sexual sense.”
The packet does not define the headword “carnal”; its source record is for “Erotomania or Eroticomania,” so the requested sense is not directly supported.
The claim that carnal means “bodily or physical in a sexual sense” is not stated in the source; the text only says the sexual feeling is “imaginative and emotional rather than carnal.”
The definition turns a contrast in the source into a positive definition of carnal, which goes beyond what the historical text supports.
